name: Stuibenfall Umhausen
kurzbeschreibung: Dropping 159 m near Umhausen in the Ötztal, Stuibenfall is Tyrol's highest waterfall, accessed via suspension bridges, 700 steps, and a via ferrata.
beschreibung:
Overview

The monumental Stuibenfall near Umhausen in the central Ötztal is by far the highest and most powerful waterfall in Tyrol, cascading down 159 meters. Formed approximately 9,000 years ago in the aftermath of a massive rockslide near Köfels, the wild Horlachbach torrent roars down two monumental tiers of rock into the valley below. The awe-inspiring natural wonder gets its name from the dense clouds of spray ('stieben') that atomise fine droplets into the canyon air. This negatively ionised water vapour has clinically proven therapeutic benefits for the respiratory system and human immunity. Thanks to a daring network of suspension bridges, cantilevered observation decks, and an exposed spiral staircase, visitors can experience the raw power of the cascading waters up close and in complete safety.

Route & Requirements

The waterfall trail begins at the spacious Bischoffsplatz car park next to the famous Ötzi Village in Umhausen. A shaded forest track leads in about 30 minutes to the base of the falls. From there, an ingenious steel walkway system featuring 700 steps and an 80-meter suspension bridge winds directly along the thunderous cataracts up to the water's source (approx. 1.5 to 2 hours ascent, 400 vertical meters, graded T2). Surefootedness, a good head for heights, and sturdy walking shoes with profile soles are essential, as the metal grates are constantly wet from spray. For climbing enthusiasts, a family-friendly via ferrata (difficulty B/C) runs parallel to the waterfall, culminating in an aerial rope bridge spanning the torrents. Scenic benches and rest spots await at the summit.

Visit & Arrival

The Stuibenfall trail is open free of charge from early May to late October (closed in winter; floodlit on summer Wednesday evenings). Drivers take the A12 Inntal motorway (exit Ötztal) and B186 to Umhausen, parking at the paid Bischoffsplatz lot. By train, travel to Ötztal-Bahnhof and catch frequent VVT regional buses to Umhausen Feuerwehr or Ötzi-Dorf. Alternatively, visitors can access the top of the falls from the mountain hamlet of Niederthai.

Tips

Combine your visit with a tour of the adjacent Ötzi Village and the Umhausen Birds of Prey Park. On Wednesday evenings during peak summer, the waterfall is illuminated by floodlights, creating a magical atmosphere as glowing water plunges into the night.
preis: Trail freely accessible free of charge (Bischoffsplatz car park fee applies)
oeffnungszeiten: Open daily from early May to late October during daylight hours (closed in winter)
saison: Mai bis Oktober (während der Wintermonate Treppenanlage gesperrt)
